FAQ - How are common names and titles determined?

Source: R/faq.R
faq-common-names.Rd

When a function builds one result from several inputs, the inputs must agree on their names and titles. If they don’t, the function errors instead of silently picking one input’s names or titles.

These functions follow the rules:

  • rray_add(), rray_subtract(), rray_multiply(), rray_divide(), and rray_exponentiate()

  • rray_and(), rray_or(), and rray_xor()

  • rray_pmax() and rray_pmin()

  • rray_combine() and rray_stack()

Rules

For each axis of the result:

All inputs with names along that axis must have exactly the same names. If all names are the same, the result has those names. If no input is named, the result is not named. If any names are different, an error is thrown to avoid arbitrarily picking between the inputs. If an input is broadcast or has no names, it is excluded from common name determination.

To resolve a conflict, preemptively remove the names from one input with rray_set_names().

Examples

Matching names are kept, and different names are an error:

x <- array(1:2, 2, dimnames = list(c("r1", "r2")))
y <- array(1:2, 2, dimnames = list(c("a", "b")))

rray_add(x, x)
#> r1 r2
#>  2  4

rray_add(x, y)
#> Error in `rray_add()`:
#> ! Can't find common names at axis 1. `x` and `y` have different names at position 1: "r1" and "a".

rray_add(x, rray_set_names(y, NULL))
#> r1 r2
#>  2  4

An input without names on an axis doesn’t participate there. Here, each input names a different axis, so both sets of names are kept:

x <- array(1:4, c(2, 2), dimnames = list(c("r1", "r2"), NULL))
y <- array(5:8, c(2, 2), dimnames = list(NULL, c("c1", "c2")))

rray_add(x, y)
#>    c1 c2
#> r1  6 10
#> r2  8 12

A broadcast axis doesn’t participate either. "total" names a single row that gets repeated, so it no longer describes the result and is dropped:

x <- array(1:3, c(1, 3), dimnames = list("total", c("a", "b", "c")))
y <- array(1:6, c(2, 3), dimnames = list(c("r1", "r2"), c("a", "b", "c")))

rray_multiply(x, y)
#>    a b  c
#> r1 1 6 15
#> r2 2 8 18

Empty names count, so c("r1", "") and c("r1", "r2") are different:

x <- array(1:2, 2, dimnames = list(c("r1", "")))
y <- array(1:2, 2, dimnames = list(c("r1", "r2")))

rray_add(x, y)
#> Error in `rray_add()`:
#> ! Can't find common names at axis 1. `x` and `y` have different names at position 2: "" and "r2".

Titles

Titles are the names of the dimension names list, like Row in list(Row = c("r1", "r2")). They label an axis rather than its positions.

For each axis of the result, all inputs with a title on that axis must have the same title, and the result gets that title. An empty title "" counts as no title. If any titles are different, an error is thrown.

x <- array(1:2, 2, dimnames = list(Row = c("r1", "r2")))
y <- array(1:2, 2, dimnames = list(Sample = c("r1", "r2")))
z <- array(1:2, 2, dimnames = list(c("r1", "r2")))

rray_add(x, y)
#> Error in `rray_add()`:
#> ! Can't find common titles at axis 1. `x` has title "Row" and `y` has title "Sample".

rray_titles(rray_add(x, z))
#> [1] "Row"

Unlike names, a title survives broadcasting, so a broadcast input still has to agree. Here the names on axis 1 are fine because x is broadcast there, but the titles are not:

x <- array(1:3, c(1, 3), dimnames = list(Row = "total", Col = c("a", "b", "c")))
y <- array(1:6, c(2, 3), dimnames = list(Sample = c("r1", "r2"), Col = c("a", "b", "c")))

rray_multiply(x, y)
#> Error in `rray_multiply()`:
#> ! Can't find common titles at axis 1. `x` has title "Row" and `y` has title "Sample".

To resolve a conflict, remove the titles from one input with rray_set_titles().

Combining and stacking

rray_combine() never checks names on .axis. They are combined from every input, with "" for inputs that have none. Titles on .axis are checked like any other axis. Every other axis follows the rules above:

a <- array(1:2, c(1, 2), dimnames = list("r1", c("x", "y")))
b <- array(3:4, c(1, 2))
c <- array(5:6, c(1, 2), dimnames = list("r3", c("x", "z")))

rray_combine(a, b, c, .axis = 1)
#> Error in `rray_combine()`:
#> ! Can't find common names at axis 2. `..1` and `..3` have different names at position 2: "y" and "z".

c <- array(5:6, c(1, 2), dimnames = list("r3", c("x", "y")))

rray_combine(a, b, c, .axis = 1)
#>    x y
#> r1 1 2
#>    3 4
#> r3 5 6

rray_stack() names the new axis with the names of ..., and gives it no title. Every other axis follows the rules above, which catches data that was reordered:

jan <- array(1:2, 2, dimnames = list(c("north", "south")))
feb <- array(3:4, 2, dimnames = list(c("south", "north")))

rray_stack(jan = jan, feb = feb, .axis = 2)
#> Error in `rray_stack()`:
#> ! Can't find common names at axis 1. `jan` and `feb` have different names at position 1: "north" and "south".

Comparisons

Comparison functions like rray_equal() and rray_greater_than() return a logical relation about their inputs rather than a new value of the input type, so they don’t return names or titles on the result and aren’t subject to these checks:

x <- array(c(TRUE, FALSE), 2, dimnames = list(c("r1", "r2")))
y <- array(c(TRUE, TRUE), 2, dimnames = list(c("a", "b")))

rray_equal(x, y)
#> [1]  TRUE FALSE
